amendments.body: In `legacy_process_param_normalization` (crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1192), the `_unit` parameter is accepted but completely ignored — normalization is purely name-based. This means if a developer attaches param_meta to `aob_k_tan_mg` with `unit = "mg total"` instead of `unit = "mg N/L"`, the system will still normalize the value to a concentration, creating a mismatch between the stated unit and the displayed value. Consider either (a) removing the unused `_unit` parameter to avoid implying it influences behavior, or (b) adding a debug assertion or warning when the attached unit doesn't match the expected normalization target (e.g., warn if a `_mg` legacy field has `unit` set to something other than a per-liter concentration).
amendments.rationale: The normalization logic is correct today given the documented convention that `valid_range` should use normalized units. But the unused `_unit` parameter creates an implicit contract that unit-awareness exists when it doesn't, which could mislead a future contributor into thinking unit-conditional normalization is already handled. Since this is a scientific codebase where unit mismatches are high-severity, surfacing a diagnostic when the unit string and the name-based normalization disagree would be a low-cost safety net.

payload.summary: The provenance schema implementation is clean and correct. `ParamMeta` (crates/tank_core/src/types/provenance.rs) provides all required fields (unit, source, confidence, valid_range, notes) with proper serde attributes for optional loading. `ConfidenceLevel` is a validated enum that rejects unknown values at deserialization. Range checking produces warnings (not errors) as required. Legacy `_mg` fields are correctly normalized via `provenance_param_value` before range checks and display formatting (dividing by the 20L reference volume). Backward compatibility is ensured by `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]` on all `param_meta` maps. All 6 acceptance criteria tests pass, plus extensive additional coverage (unknown key rejection, non-finite values, invalid ranges, preset-level vs per-parameter confidence distinction, normalization display). The `deny_unknown_fields` on `ParamMeta` correctly prevents the `value` field from leaking into metadata sections. The `ParamMetaPreset` trait provides a clean abstraction for range checking and formatting across all preset types. Only one minor design concern identified (unused `_unit` parameter in normalization).
